ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the diagram, point \(P\) is the centroid of \(\triangle ABC\). Through point \(P\), draw \(DE\parallel AC\) intersecting \(BC, AB\) at \(D, E\) respectively, and \(EF\parallel BC\) intersecting \(AC\) at point \(F\). If \(BC=11\), what is the length of \(EF\)?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
Solution: Connect BP extending it to meet AC at point G,\\
since DE$\parallel$AC, and EF$\parallel$BC,\\
thus quadrilateral EFCD is a parallelogram,\\
therefore EF=CD;\\
since point P is the centroid,\\
therefore $\frac{BP}{PG}=2$,\\
since ED$\parallel$AC,\\
thus $\frac{BP}{PG}=\frac{BD}{CD}=2$,\\
therefore $\frac{BD}{EF}=2$\\
since BD+CD=BC=11 which implies 2EF+EF=11\\
Solving gives: $EF=\boxed{\frac{11}{3}}$

ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: In the figure is triangle ABC, A is above, B is at the lower left, C is at the lower right, and BC is the base. Point E is on AB, point F is on AC, and EF is drawn as a line segment parallel to the base BC. Point D is on BC, line segment ED passes through the interior point P, and ED is parallel to the direction of side AC. P is marked inside the triangle, and the problem statement explains that P is the centroid of triangle ABC. Reasoning: According to the method, connect BP and extend it to intersect AC at G. Because P is the centroid of triangle ABC, G is the midpoint of AC, and the centroid on the median satisfies BP:PG=2:1, therefore BP:BG=2:3. Also because D, P, E are collinear, and DE∥AC, so PD∥GC. In triangle BGC, PD∥GC, therefore triangle BPD and triangle BGC are similar. From the similarity ratio, BD:BC=BP:BG=2:3, so BD=2/3×11=22/3, and then DC=BC-BD=11-22/3=11/3. From the figure and the meaning of the problem, it can be known that EF∥BC, so EF∥DC; also ED∥AC, so ED∥FC. Therefore quadrilateral EFCD is a parallelogram, hence EF=CD=11/3.
